text.arabic_uthmani: إِنْ أَحْسَنتُمْ أَحْسَنتُمْ لِأَنفُسِكُمْ ۖ وَإِنْ أَسَأْتُمْ فَلَهَا ۚ فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعْدُ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ لِيَسُۥٓـُٔوا۟ وُجُوهَكُمْ وَلِيَدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْمَسْجِدَ كَمَا دَخَلُوهُ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍۢ وَلِيُتَبِّرُوا۟ مَا عَلَوْا۟ تَتْبِيرًا

words.gloss_range: open conditional particle launching a live moral choice rather than a counterfactual report
words.prose: {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) opens with conditional address. With the following perfect verb, it frames the choice as a completable act whose consequence can be mirrored immediately, so the restored interval becomes a serious testing space without making the warning fatalistic.

topics.headline: open conditional accountability
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah begins from live accountability, not from a closed fate.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: Form IV active doing or producing of good, where moral excellence and beauty oppose produced harm
words.root_gloss_range: beauty, goodness, rightness, and excellence; locally Form IV makes goodness an active production
words.prose: {{ar:أَحْسَنتُمْ}} ({{tr:ahsantum}}) names the addressees as producers of good. Its beauty-and-excellence field stands opposite the later harm-root, and that lexical contrast is matched by directional consequence: benefit toward the selves versus harm rebounding back. Its exact repetition makes the good act echo back toward the same selves.

topics.headline: active produced goodness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices goodness as an active production by the addressed group, with beauty-versus-harm and benefit-versus-rebound both built into the opening contrast.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: repeated Form IV apodosis that turns doing good into its own self-directed result
words.root_gloss_range: beauty, goodness, rightness, and excellence; locally the repeated Form IV turns the act back toward its doers
words.prose: The second {{ar:أَحْسَنتُمْ}} ({{tr:ahsantum}}) occupies the answer slot. Because the apodosis repeats the condition verb, the good action is made to return as settled benefit for its own doers.

topics.headline: returned good as apodosis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the consequence is stated by repeating the act itself rather than by naming an external reward.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: beneficiary lām routing the repeated good action toward the addressees own selves
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) gives the answer its direction. The bound preposition makes the selves the recipients of the good action before the following noun is complete, and it prepares the later reversal where the same directional shape carries harm back onto that domain.

topics.headline: beneficiary direction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices self-benefit as a grammatical relation, not merely an implication.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: the addressees own collective selves as beneficiary domain, including inner, moral, and embodied selfhood
words.root_gloss_range: self, soul, person, breath, and appetite; locally the addressees own selves are the beneficiary domain
words.prose: {{ar:أَنفُسِكُمْ}} ({{tr:anfusikum}}) makes the beneficiary personal and collective. The suffix binds the return to the same addressed group, while the root range lets selfhood include person, soul, and appetite without replacing the local beneficiary sense.

topics.headline: owned collective selves
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the benefit returning to the whole owned self of the same addressed group.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction giving the harmful alternative equal syntactic rank with the good alternative
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) coordinates the second condition with the first. Good and evil are placed in one balanced moral frame, and the same coordination sets self-benefit against self-harm rather than leaving the clauses unrelated.

topics.headline: coordinated moral binary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the harmful path as the parallel counterpart to the good path, setting self-benefit and self-harm inside one coordinated binary.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: second open conditional particle mirroring the first while introducing the harmful path
words.prose: The second {{ar:إِنْ}} ({{tr:in}}) repeats the conditional architecture for evil. The harmful path remains possible but not predetermined, and it is measured in the same frame as good.

topics.headline: mirrored second condition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that both moral paths are framed as live choices under the same grammar.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: Form IV active causing of harm or ugliness, opposite produced goodness and later echoed as visible punishment
words.root_gloss_range: evil, harm, ugliness, and disgrace; locally Form IV makes harm an active production opposite goodness
words.prose: {{ar:أَسَأْتُمْ}} ({{tr:asaʾtum}}) reverses the good root with a matching Form IV verb. The evil act is presented as complete in itself, ready for the compact rebound that follows, and the harm-root later returns in the face-marring verb as moral ugliness made visible.

topics.headline: active produced harm
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same addressees actively producing harm as a complete condition, whose ugliness later becomes visible punishment.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: causal apodosis marker that makes evil rebound abruptly and asymmetrically
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) marks the answer to the evil condition as a triggered result. Unlike the good half, the harmful path receives an abrupt directional rebound.

topics.headline: causal evil rebound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices evil consequence as a marked rebound triggered by the condition.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: compact preposition-pronoun rebound, with detriment and self/deed reference pressure kept live
words.prose: {{ar:لَهَا}} ({{tr:lahā}}) compresses the evil result into one rebound unit. The lām that earlier marked benefit now points toward detriment, and the feminine pronoun keeps both the selves and the evil deed in play.

topics.headline: compact detrimental rebound
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that harm remains inside the addressees own domain whether heard through the self or the deed.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: resumptive fā pivoting from moral binary into the temporal promise sequence
words.prose: The next {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) changes function. It resumes the discourse and pivots from moral axiom into the timed arrival of the promise and its three-purpose sequence.

topics.headline: resumptive hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the verse turning from conditional accountability into narrated consequence.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: temporal adverb marking expected arrival, shifting from if-choice to when-event
words.prose: {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) changes the modal feel of the verse. The opening choices were framed with if; the promise is framed as when, so contingency gives way to expected arrival.

topics.headline: when not if
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the promised event is expected, not another open option.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: perfect intransitive arrival of the promise itself, making the event grammatically certain
words.root_gloss_range: coming, arriving, and bringing; locally the promise itself arrives as subject
words.prose: {{ar:جَآءَ}} ({{tr:jāʾa}}) makes the promise arrive as the subject of the scene. The perfect form gives certainty, and the intransitive frame makes the promise become operative rather than be brought as an object.

topics.headline: promise arrives
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the promise as the arriving subject and active event participant.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: verbal noun promise as arriving subject, bound to the latter/final event and carrying threat force
words.root_gloss_range: promise, appointment, and threat; locally a promised punitive event arrives
words.prose: {{ar:وَعْدُ}} ({{tr:waʿdu}}) is the subject that comes. As a verbal noun in construct with the latter/final term, it holds promise, appointment, and threat together as the event that drives the clause.

topics.headline: arriving promise-threat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices promise certainty and threatening content held together in one arriving nominal event.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: definite genitive latter/final term completing the promise phrase with historical and final-outcome resonance
words.root_gloss_range: delay, lastness, laterness, and final outcome; locally the latter promise carries final-outcome resonance
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ}} ({{tr:al-ākhirah}}) completes the promise phrase as the latter or final term. Locally it points to the second promised occasion, but its delay-and-lastness image makes that promise feel held back until its appointed arrival, while its final-outcome register and recurrence at 17:104 widen the resonance.

topics.headline: latter and final overlap
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the local second promise worded with final-outcome pressure and echoed again at 17:104.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: first purpose lām governing the face-marring verb and launching the three-purpose chain
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) begins the purpose chain. It marks the first punishment verb as intended within the promise arrival, with the purpose prefix fused to the harm verb on the surface, and sets up the repeated lām pattern for entry and destruction.

topics.headline: first purpose lām
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices face-marring as a stated purpose in a coordinated chain.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: subjunctive harm verb in the first purpose clause, locally selecting face-marring while variants expose agency pressure
words.root_gloss_range: evil, harm, ugliness, and distress; locally the face object selects visible marring or public disgrace
words.prose: {{ar:يَسُۥٓـُٔوا۟}} ({{tr:yasūʾū}}) is the first verb in the purpose triad. With faces as object, the harm-root narrows to visible marring and public disgrace; variant readings keep agency pressure visible without replacing the local chain.

topics.headline: visible harm and agency pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices visible face-harm as the stable payoff while variant readings expose agency as the pressure point.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: plural possessed faces as the visible object of harm, carrying literal face and orientation pressure
words.root_gloss_range: face, front, direction, aspect, and orientation; locally faces are the visible harmed object
words.prose: {{ar:وُجُوهَكُمْ}} ({{tr:wujūhakum}}) is where the first punishment lands. The plural suffix keeps the same addressees in view, while the face/front range makes the harm public: faces, orientation, and corporate standing are disturbed.

topics.headline: faces as public object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices punishment first landing on the public-facing surface of the same addressed group.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction keeping the second lām-purpose clause inside the same chain
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) keeps the entry clause coordinated with the face-marring clause. The sequence does not restart; it adds a second purpose inside the same escalation.

topics.headline: second purpose coordination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sanctuary entry as the next coordinated purpose, not a detached scene.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: second purpose lām making sanctuary entry an intentional middle stage of the triad
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) marks entry as purpose, not incident. As the middle lām, it balances the chain between visible disgrace and final destruction.

topics.headline: middle purpose lām
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices sacred-space entry as an intended middle stage between humiliation and destruction.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: purpose-governed entry into the definite sanctuary, a boundary crossing mirrored by earlier entry
words.root_gloss_range: entering, inward crossing, and penetration; locally entry breaches the definite sanctuary space
words.prose: {{ar:يَدْخُلُوا۟}} ({{tr:yadkhulū}}) makes the second purpose a breach of space. The root selects concrete entry into the definite sanctuary, and the later perfect comparison makes the future action answer a completed template.

topics.headline: sacred boundary entry
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a breach of protected submission-space, not generic movement.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: definite place of prostration as entered object, identifiable from the surah opening
words.root_gloss_range: bowing and prostrating in bodily submission; locally the place noun names a site of prostration
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمَسْجِدَ}} ({{tr:al-masjida}}) gives the middle purpose a concrete sacred center. Its definiteness points to an identifiable sanctuary with the surah opening as an anchor (17:1), and as a place noun from the prostration root, the space defined by bodily submission becomes the object of entry and violation.

topics.headline: definite prostration site
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the entered object is a prostration-site and identifiable sanctuary anchored by the surah opening (17:1), not a neutral building.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: comparison particle linking the future entry to the earlier entry template
words.prose: {{ar:كَ}} ({{tr:ka}}) begins the comparison that makes the future entry intelligible through a past one. Its compact comparative role creates a temporal loop inside the entry clause.

topics.headline: comparison of entries
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second entry is patterned after an earlier entry.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: mā inside the comparative construction, allowing the past entry to function as event and manner standard
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) turns the following past-entry clause into the standard of comparison. It can point to the event of entering and to the manner of that entry.

topics.headline: event and manner standard
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the comparison measuring both the fact of earlier entry and its manner.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: perfect past entry with object suffix pointing back to the masjid as template for future entry
words.root_gloss_range: entering and inward crossing; locally a completed entry into the same sanctuary object
words.prose: {{ar:دَخَلُوهُ}} ({{tr:dakhalūhu}}) supplies the completed past template. Its suffix points back to the same sanctuary, keeping the comparison anchored rather than generic, and the repeated entry-root makes the earlier template another boundary crossing of that sacred space.

topics.headline: completed entry template
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices recurrence: the promised entry is described through what already happened to the same sanctuary.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: ordinal first as temporal accusative, making the past entry a counted origin-instance in a cycle
words.root_gloss_range: firstness, origin, and return; locally the ordinal marks the first occurrence
words.prose: {{ar:أَوَّلَ}} ({{tr:awwala}}) locates the comparison at the first occurrence. The ordinal counts the instance and also carries origin-and-return pressure in the cycle of entries.

topics.headline: first occurrence frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the earlier entry as a counted first occurrence that folds time back toward an origin template.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: single-instance occasion completing the first-time phrase with passage and bitterness pressure
words.root_gloss_range: passing, occurrence, and bitterness; locally a single occasion with secondary bitter-passage pressure
words.prose: {{ar:مَرَّةٍۢ}} ({{tr:marratin}}) completes the first-time expression as one counted occurrence. Its instance form retrieves the two-occasion frame from 17:4, while passage and bitterness color the occasion without replacing the local sense.

topics.headline: single bitter occasion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first occurrence as one counted occasion that retrieves the twofold decree at 17:4.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: final coordinating conjunction keeping destruction parallel while making it the climactic third purpose
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) introduces the third purpose without breaking parallel governance. It keeps destruction coordinated with marring and entry while moving the chain to its climax.

topics.headline: climactic coordination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices destruction as the third coordinated purpose, not an afterthought.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: third purpose lām governing the intensive destruction verb and opening the closure movement
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) marks total destruction as the final stated purpose. As the last lām in the refrain, it channels the sequence toward emphatic closure.

topics.headline: final purpose lām
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices total destruction as grammatically intended within the chain.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: purpose-governed Form II destruction verb, intensive and rare, climaxing before its cognate accusative
words.root_gloss_range: shattering and utter destruction; locally Form II intensifies deliberate annihilation
words.prose: {{ar:يُتَبِّرُوا۟}} ({{tr:yutabbirū}}) is the heaviest verb in the triad. Its Form II shape intensifies the rare destruction root, moving beyond damage toward shattering organized dominance back into raw, unusable ruin before the cognate noun doubles the effect.

topics.headline: intensive destruction verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices destruction as deliberate shattering of formed order back toward raw, unusable ruin, not mere damage.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: open relative object of destruction, naming whatever domain they had risen over
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) opens the object field instead of naming a target. The destruction reaches whatever they had dominated, and total scope appears before the dominance verb defines it.

topics.headline: open destruction scope
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the target of destruction as comprehensive rather than itemized.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: plural past dominance verb qualifying the open object as whatever height or dominion they attained
words.root_gloss_range: height, rising, superiority, dominance, and exaltedness; locally human dominance becomes destructible height
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَوْا۟}} ({{tr:ʿalaw}}) defines the open object as what they had risen over or dominated. The height-root keeps the image physical and moral: attained elevation becomes the field marked for destruction.

topics.headline: destructible height
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices domination as a destructible height, with 17:4 arrogance becoming the field undone.
topics.reason: The CRITICAL rows for this word converge on the stated local payoff, and the QAC, attachment, contextual, and V4 evidence keep it anchored to the local grammar and surface.

words.gloss_range: cognate accusative verbal noun that intensifies and names final destruction as total ruin
words.root_gloss_range: shattering and utter destruction; locally the verbal noun intensifies the preceding verb as total ruin
words.prose: {{ar:تَتْبِيرًا}} ({{tr:tatbīran}}) lands the ayah on destruction itself. As a cognate accusative, it adds no new object; it confirms the manner and totality of the preceding verb as emphatic ruin.

topics.headline: emphatic total ruin
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah ending not merely with an action but with destruction as a named terminal state.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired conditionals repeat حسن and reuse سوء, while لأنفسكم and فلها direct both consequences back to the addressed selves.
baseline_models.mechanism: Good action recursively accrues to the actor; bad action returns likewise, and the second سوء occurrence externalizes that return on the face.

activation_trace.role: The repeated causative action supplies deliberate beneficence as both input and self-directed yield.
Self as the actor's own identity makes the beneficiary and liability holder coincide.
Harm links the initial wrongdoing to the later making-bad of the face, closing the return circuit.

changed_reading.before: Good helps the doer and evil harms the doer.
changed_reading.after: Conduct is a reflexive circuit: the deed accrues to the self, and evil later becomes publicly legible on that same collective self.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The latter promise arrives, and the entry is explicitly compared with a first occurrence.
baseline_models.mechanism: A bounded appointment materializes as a replay: latter and first distinguish turns, while the doubled دخول and temporal مرة make the prior incursion a reusable pattern.

activation_trace.role: Arrival turns the announced event from latent commitment into present occurrence.
A bounded appointment supplies the temporal threshold that releases the sequence.
Lateness distinguishes this turn from an earlier counterpart without erasing their relation.
The repeated ingress verb makes penetration of the interior the event copied across turns.
The first occurrence supplies the template against which the latter entry is recognized.
An occurrence counted in time converts similarity into recurrence.

changed_reading.before: A promised enemy attack happens again.
changed_reading.after: The latter promise is an appointed replay: arrival reopens a prior ingress pattern, so history is structured as repeatable turns rather than an isolated raid.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Three purpose clauses move from faces, to entry into the mosque, to destroying whatever the entrants overtop.
baseline_models.mechanism: Damage advances by depth and scale: it first marks the visible front, then breaches the ritual interior, then dismantles the order brought under domination.

activation_trace.role: The visible front of the person is the first site on which the consequence appears.
Ingress carries the action from exposed surface into a bounded interior.
The prayer-place makes the breached interior communal and sacred rather than merely architectural.
Overtaking and domination define the full reach of what becomes exposed to destruction.
Intensive breaking and nullification make the terminal phase structural rather than momentary.

changed_reading.before: Attackers humiliate people, enter the mosque, and destroy possessions.
changed_reading.after: The punishment advances by depth: public countenance is spoiled, sacred interior is breached, and the attained upper order is dismantled.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: Faces are made bad immediately before elevated dominance is subjected to intensive destruction.
baseline_models.mechanism: Moral defect becomes public discredit: the wrongdoing root returns as marked disgrace, while faces as bearers of standing and domineering elevation are reversed together.

activation_trace.role: Making defective and blameworthy translates prior wrongdoing into an exposed mark.
Face as public standing lets bodily humiliation also register as loss of rank and leadership.
Domineering elevation supplies the high social order exposed to reversal.
Thorough nullification converts discredit into the collapse of elevated power.

changed_reading.before: Their faces are physically grieved or disfigured before material destruction.
changed_reading.after: The sequence can also stage a political reversal: public standing is disgraced before an order built on overbearing elevation is undone.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus is the hinge of an explicit two-turn feedback loop: loss of order triggers an appointed incursion, restored capacity reopens agency, and renewed return can meet either mercy or renewed response.

activation_trace.role: The latter appointment is the threshold at which accumulated conduct becomes an event.
Reference to the first occurrence keeps the present turn inside a repeated series.
Departure from sound order names the recurrent state that initiates both turns.
Restoration of the counterturn interrupts defeat and proves that the communal state can reverse.
Merciful tenderness keeps a restorative outcome open after punishment.
Paired return after departure makes renewed conduct elicit renewed response.

structural_cues: 17:4 announces two occurrences; 17:5 fulfills the first promise; 17:7 names the latter and repeats the first entry.
17:6 restores the turn and resources, while 17:8 pairs return with return and leaves mercy possible.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies explicit two, first, latter, restoration, and paired-return markers plus a mercy branch; I infer a conduct-response feedback loop in which communal state changes the next turn. A live alternative is a closed historical chronology with no reusable mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The ayah states individual moral reciprocity and then reports a second invasion.
changed_reading.after: The moral conditional is the control rule of a communal cycle: conduct changes the group's condition, the appointed response arrives, recovery restores agency, and recurrence remains conditional rather than fatalistic.

context_deltas.mechanism: Guidance directs intentional work toward uprightness and repair, whose reward returns to its makers; حسن therefore becomes self-building alignment rather than an unspecified pleasant deed.

activation_trace.role: Deliberate beneficence anchors the focus side of a constructive action sequence.
Gentle direction toward a true path supplies orientation before action.
Straightness and balanced standing define the order toward which guidance aims.
Purposive work turns orientation into enacted construction.
Soundness opposed to corruption identifies the work's restorative product.
Return for work completes the constructive circuit back to the actors.

structural_cues: 17:9 links guidance, the most upright course, intentional sound works, and a large return in one chain.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an orientation-work-soundness-return chain; I map that chain onto the focus's repeated حسن and its benefit to the self. The live alternative is that 17:9 only states a neighboring reward proposition and does not specify حسن.

changed_reading.after: Doing good is self-repair through guided, intentional alignment: it builds the sound order and capacity that corruption later places at risk.

context_deltas.mechanism: Haste can put the same desiring or calling force behind opposite outcomes, so the focus's good and bad poles cannot be reduced to what the actor urgently names or wants.

activation_trace.role: Deliberate good action supplies one pole whose identity initially appears self-evident.
Badness and defect supply the opposed pole and its adverse yield.
A call capable of bringing an unwelcome outcome gives desire a self-harming causal route.
Explicit evil occupies the object slot of the same calling pattern used for good.
Desired benefit supplies the comparison pole that makes the inversion visible.
Premature acceleration explains how desire can outrun discrimination between the two outcomes.

structural_cues: 17:11 places evil and good after parallel calling constructions and closes by characterizing the human as hasty.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies syntactic equivalence between calling for evil and good plus haste; I infer that haste can corrupt an actor's classification of what benefits the self. A live alternative confines the warning to impulsive speech rather than moral discernment generally.

changed_reading.before: The actor knows which deeds are good and which are bad, and each produces its matching consequence.
changed_reading.after: The consequence rule remains stable, but human labeling is unstable: urgency may pursue harm under the felt form of benefit, so desire is not the measure of حسن.

context_deltas.mechanism: Acts become entries attached to the acting self: the record adheres, the self reckons it, and its burden cannot migrate to another bearer.

activation_trace.role: The actor's own identity anchors both benefit and liability in the focus.
Binding a judgment to its subject supplies the attachment rule for the personal record.
The self as one's very identity becomes sufficient witness to its own account.
Counting and reckoning convert accumulated conduct into an inspectable account.
The repeated benefit-to-self construction directly echoes and sharpens the focus.
A heavy load assigned to its bearer supplies the nontransferability of adverse consequence.

structural_cues: 17:13 fastens a record to each person, and 17:14 makes the self sufficient as reckoner.
17:15 repeats benefit to one's own self and liability upon it, then bars one bearer from carrying another's burden.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies attachment, self-reckoning, a near-exact self-benefit/self-liability echo, and nontransferable burden; I infer a personal ledger joining them. A live alternative reads the focus only as immediate psychosocial consequence without a stored account.

changed_reading.before: Good and evil rebound upon their doers.
changed_reading.after: Every deed posts to a self-held, nontransferable account: the same self receives the gain, bears the load, and ultimately reads the record.

context_deltas.mechanism: Counted time, the contrast between immediate and latter aims, purposeful striving, and graded outcomes let the focus's latter promise retain its second-event sense while also opening a delayed moral horizon.

activation_trace.role: A fixed time capable of recurrence makes the promise legible as a scheduled moral threshold.
What comes after the first supplies both sequence and semantic openness toward a later horizon.
Enumeration turns passing years into measurable intervals rather than undifferentiated delay.
Acceleration and bringing forward define the immediate horizon against which later consequence is read.
The explicit later aim reactivates the focus term beyond the local first-versus-second pairing.
Purposeful movement toward an aim links delayed outcome to sustained agency.
Stepwise levels make the later result differentiated rather than a single undivided endpoint.

structural_cues: 17:12 makes day and night signs for counting years and reckoning.
17:18 and 17:19 oppose the immediate aim to the latter aim, and 17:21 describes the latter in larger degrees.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies counted time, an explicit immediate/latter contrast, striving, and degrees; I allow that later semantic horizon to resonate in 17:7 while preserving the local second-incursion sense. A live alternative keeps 17:7's term exclusively ordinal.

changed_reading.before: The latter promise means only the second of two historical incursions.
changed_reading.after: The second incursion remains primary, but it also becomes a near-field instance of delayed moral accounting: immediate choices mature across counted time into differentiated latter outcomes.

context_deltas.mechanism: Expansive privilege releases boundary-breaking conduct inside a settlement; fixed liability and total demolition follow, making the invaders' destruction the terminal phase of an internally compromised order.

activation_trace.role: Overbearing elevation identifies the kind of high order whose own posture helps expose it to reversal.
Intensive nullification is the visible terminal operation performed on that order.
Falling into extinction supplies the endpoint toward which the settlement sequence moves.
Abundance that releases its possessor supplies the internal social condition preceding breach.
Emergence outside a containing skin gives the transgression a boundary-breaking material image.
Extirpating ruin confirms that the endpoint is systemic removal, not a limited setback.
Culpability ties repeated generational destruction back to the inhabitants' own conduct.

structural_cues: 17:16 sequences privileged actors, their breach, fixed liability, and intensive demolition inside one settlement.
17:17 broadens destruction across generations and explicitly joins it to culpability.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the internal sequence from privilege through breach to demolition and then generalizes destruction by culpability; I infer that external unmaking executes the collapse of an already compromised order. A live alternative treats the sequence only juridically, without an endogenous social mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Enemy forces destroy whatever they manage to overrun.
changed_reading.after: Their destructive entry is the terminal unmaking of an order destabilized from within: expansive privilege breaks containment, domineering height becomes vulnerable, and external force completes the collapse.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it links the focus to the distant opening movement rather than only to the immediate historical sequence. It remains anchored by repeated mosque-space, directed movement, entry, seeing, and faces; downstream prose should present it as a compositional reversal, not as a claim that the two journeys are lexically equivalent.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The hostile agents enter the mosque and alter faces, while the opening context moves a servant between mosque-spaces in order to be shown signs.

activation_trace.role: The communal prayer-place is the shared spatial anchor across the two movements.
Hostile ingress turns access to sacred interior into penetration.
The exposed face lets the later movement terminate in public visibility and injury.
Directed night travel supplies the opening's protected sacred transit.
Two prayer-places frame movement as passage within a sacred spatial relation.
Being shown signs gives the opening transit a revelatory visual end opposed to later facial exposure.

changed_reading.before: The focus reports a repeated hostile entry into a mosque and humiliation of faces.
changed_reading.after: Against the opening sacred passage toward seeing signs, the later entry reads as reversed transit: access becomes penetration, and revelatory seeing becomes exposed, injured countenance.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is branch-distant because it activates a split mapped root's alternating annual yield rather than the dominant promise sense. It remains anchored by the paired conditionals and the first/latter recurrence markers; downstream prose should qualify it as a temporal-material analogy, never as a replacement translation for وعد.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The two moral conditions precede a latter appointment explicitly patterned on a first occurrence.

activation_trace.role: Alternating productive and fallow years supply an image for conduct yielding opposite communal seasons.
A counted time that comes around again supplies the clock for alternation.
The latter phase marks the second side of the alternating pattern.
The first phase supplies the prior season to which the later one answers.
Counted occurrence keeps the analogy periodic rather than merely oppositional.

changed_reading.before: Good and evil produce consequences, followed by the second promised incursion.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the ayah resembles an alternating-yield clock: collective conduct bears one season, lapses into another, and the counted turn returns with its corresponding fruit.

strongest_changes: The focus became the hinge of an explicit conduct-response cycle rather than a detached maxim followed by a raid.
The self-directed clauses became a nontransferable ledger through the attached record, self-reckoning, and burden syntax of 17:13-15.
The good-and-bad polarity became epistemically unstable under haste: desired benefit can be misidentified even though the consequence rule remains stable.
The latter promise retained its second-incursion sense while also resonating with counted time, delayed striving, and graded latter outcomes.
summary.what_was_special: The same سوء root joins prior wrongdoing to later facial injury, while the purpose clauses move from visible face through sacred interior to dominated height. Context then supplies unusually exact return, self-accounting, and immediate-versus-latter mechanisms instead of merely thematic parallels.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether faces primarily denote bodily grief or disfigurement, public standing, leading persons, or several of these at once.
Whether the later horizon activated by 17:18-21 should remain a resonance or materially govern the focus's ordinal use.
Whether ما علوا centers what the entrants physically overtop, the power they dominate, or an already elevated social order.
Whether the alternating-yield split-root activation is productive enough for downstream prose or should remain trace-only.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Action loops back into the acting self.** `ح س ن:B002` is beneficent skilled action, `ن ف س:B011/B013` the living self and hidden intent, and `س و ء:B001/B002` ugliness and harm. Exact repetition of *aḥsantum* and pronominal return to the self produce a feedback structure, echoed in 17:15 and 17:19. I infer acts reshape the agent before their external return. The opening reads as moral self-construction, not only later reward or penalty.
2. **Elevated control is broken into unusable fragments.** `ع ل و:B004/B008` gives mastery and what lies on top, while doubled `ت ب ر:B001/B002` gives destruction and raw fragments. Entry repeats the first incursion and terminates in pulverizing what had been mastered; 17:49–51 later turns bones, dust, stone, and iron into material images of re-creation. I infer domination's built surfaces become the material of dismantling. The close reads as deliberate deconstruction of the apparatus of ascent.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:97–98 unexpectedly embody the same feedback principle: covered signs return as disabled face, sight, speech, and hearing. The opening self-return became a surah-wide causal law.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Destruction as material deconstruction of the superstructure.** Lexical evidence: `ت ب ر B002` (raw, unworked mineral or fragments) in doubled `لِيُتَبِّرُوا۟ ... تَتْبِيرًا`, and `ع ل و B008` (what is on top or added above) in `مَا عَلَوْا۟`. Structural cue: 17:5 penetrates interstices, while 17:12 will distinguish signs and `فَصَّلْنَٰهُ تَفْصِيلًا`; entry precedes the destruction of what was built above. Assigned role: the fragment branch specifies the material result and the upper-addition branch specifies the target. Abductive move: fragmentation is lexically available but not stated as a construction process; I infer that interior penetration enables dismantling from organized height into pieces. Reading change: `تتبير` becomes the unmaking of an elevated order down to its raw remainder, not only an abstract defeat.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 17:12 unexpectedly activated the fragment-image of `ت ب ر B002`: its doubled detailing/separation made 17:7's destruction look like reduction of an elevated construction into parts.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_channel: P1 (17:1-22): Directed Passage Through Bounded Fields
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: A directed movement crosses distance while boundaries, stations, and a receiving field give the movement its intelligible course.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The sacred itinerary materializes as a hydraulic system in which a current is routed, collected, replenished, and turned around a fixed basin.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Routed Current and Receiving Basin
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Water is led through a channel, flows into a fixed pool, is reinforced by another current, and can be circulated by a lifting device.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: routed watercourse (`quranic:root_000009:B004/m01`); running current (`quranic:root_000702:B002/m01`); fixed pool (`quranic:root_000109:B003/m01`); water collected in a depression (`quranic:root_000281:B003/m01`); gathered water (`quranic:root_001292:B003/m01`); replenishing flow (`quranic:root_001407:B003/m01`); river channel (`quranic:root_001559:B001/m01`); water-lifting mechanism (`quranic:root_000373:B016/m01`)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The lexical field converts directed passage into fluid conveyance. An incoming stream is given a course, received in a basin, augmented by a second supply, and kept moving by a turning apparatus. This makes the opening journey resonate as controlled transmission into a prepared sacred surround rather than motion through undifferentiated space.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Collective force moves through openings, meets a reversal, and is finally contained by the consequences of repeated return.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: Military recurrence is rendered through apertures, repeated rotations, gathered force, and a woven or enclosing final boundary.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Penetration Through the Dwellings
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A threatened appointment activates a dispatched force that searches through gaps, enters inhabited space, and shatters what it overtakes.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: threatening promise (`quranic:root_001662:B002/m01`); bounded appointment (`quranic:root_001662:B003/m01`); dispatched agent (`quranic:root_000129:B002/m01`); collective surge (`quranic:root_000129:B004/m01`); overpowering force (`quranic:root_000079:B001/m01`); penetration through dwellings (`quranic:root_000277:B001/m01`); trampling mixture with a place (`quranic:root_000277:B003/m01`); interstitial opening (`quranic:root_000435:B001/m01`); entry (`quranic:root_000464:B001/m01`); annihilating breakage (`quranic:root_000174:B001/m01`)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The scene has a precise assault geometry. The promise fixes the activation point; dispatch and force provide the agents; gaps and interiors supply the route; penetration becomes physical mixture with the occupied place; and breakage is the outcome. The latent spatial mechanics intensify the surface account of invasion.

identity_judgment.rationale: Dalın çirkinliğin karşıtı olan güzel ve beğenilir niteliğe ilişkin çerçevesi, kaynak söz öbeğiyle örtüşür. Bu nitelik yalnızca dış görünüşe bağlı değildir; aklın, kişisel eğilimin veya duyuların olumlu bulduğu şeyleri, kişilerdeki yoğun güzelliği ve bir kişi ya da şeydeki güzel yanları da kapsar.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal bir nitelik ve durum bildirir; başkasına iyilik etme eylemini, kişiye ulaşan iyi sonucu veya kalıplaşmış özel adlandırmaları kapsamaz.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dalın yalın kapsamı güzel ve beğenilir olma niteliğidir; belirli bir söz öbeğine özgü eylem veya sonuç anlamı bu kapsama taşınmamalıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin, şeyin, görünüşün veya niteliğin; akıl, kişisel eğilim ya da duyular bakımından güzel ve beğenilir bulunması, dolayısıyla çirkinliğin ve kötü yanların karşısında yer almasıdır.

facets.statement: Bir kişi veya şeyin güzel ve beğenilir olması, çirkinliğin karşıtı olan temel anlamdır.
Olumlu değerlendirme akla, kişisel eğilime veya duyulara dayanabilir; dal yalnızca görsel güzellikle sınırlı değildir.
İnsanlar güzel diye nitelenebilir ve aynı nitelik çok yüksek derecede güzelliği belirten biçimlerle güçlendirilebilir.
Bir insanın, işin veya başka bir şeyin güzel yerleri ve iyi nitelikleri, onun kötü yanlarının karşıtı olarak topluca anılabilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, temel karşıtlığı güzel ile çirkin arasında kurar; güzel olmayı kişi ve şeylere yüklenen bir nitelik olarak verir. Toplu anlatım ayrıca akla, eğilime ve duyulara göre beğenilirliği, yoğun güzelliği ve güzel yanların kötü yanlara karşıtlığını kapsar.

concept_gloss.text: akla, eğilime veya duyulara göre güzel ve beğenilir olma
concept_gloss.applicability: Dalın kişi, şey, görünüş ve niteliklerdeki ortak çekirdeğini, olumlu değerlendirmenin farklı dayanaklarını silmeden karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Güzel olmayı, beğenilirliği, değerlendirme yollarını ve çirkinliğe karşıtlığı birlikte korur.

error_profile.loses: Akla veya kişisel eğilime dayanan daha geniş beğenilirlik alanını tek başına açıkça göstermez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir şeyin görünüşünden çok akıl, istek veya değerlendirme bakımından olumlu bulunduğu bağlamlarda uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Bir şeyin olumlu bulunması ve istenir görülmesi yönünü korur.
error_profile.loses: Kişinin veya bedenin somut güzelliğini ve güzelliğin çok yüksek derecesini açıkça belirtmez.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişi, iş veya şeydeki güzel yerler ile iyi niteliklerin topluca kötü yanlarla karşılaştırıldığı kullanım içindir.

error_profile.preserves: Çoğul güzel yerleri ve iyi nitelikleri kötü yanların karşıtı olarak eksiksiz korur.
Olumlu değerlendirme ve beğenilirlik yönünden sınırlı bir ortaklık taşır.
error_profile.loses: Görünüşteki güzelliği, yoğun güzelliği ve güzel yanların çirkinliğe karşıtlığını siler.

identity_judgment.rationale: Dal çerçevesi, kaynak söz öbeğinde bulunan başkasına iyilik etme ve kişinin kendi işini iyi yapma yönlerini birlikte korur. Bir şeyi güzelleştirme, eylemi ustalıkla yürütme, kötülüğün karşısında iyi davranma ve karşılık denkliğini aşan iyilik de bu eylemsel çekirdeğin ayrı görünümleridir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal güzel bir niteliğin kendisini değil, güzelleştiren, iyi yapan veya bir başkasına yarar sağlayan eylemi anlatır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal belirli bir söz öbeğine bağlı değildir; genel eylem alanı, başkasına yarar sağlama ile işi iyi ve özenli yapma yönleri ayrılarak tanımlanmalıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi güzelleştirmek, bir işi iyi ve özenli biçimde yapmak ya da bir başkasına yarar sağlayan bir iyilikte bulunmaktır. Başkasına yönelik biçimi, yalnızca denk bir karşılık vermenin ötesine geçen artırılmış bir iyilik içerebilir.

facets.statement: Kötü davranmanın karşısında yer alan iyi ve güzel eylem, dalın ortak eylemsel çekirdeğidir.
Eylem bir başkasına yöneldiğinde ona yarar sağlama, iyilik etme veya iyi davranma biçimini alır.
Eylem kişinin kendi işine yöneldiğinde işi iyi, doğru ve ustalıkla yapmayı belirtir.
Bir şeyi daha güzel duruma getirme, iyi eylemin nesne üzerinde sonuç doğuran biçimidir.
İyilik etme, kimi kullanımda yalnızca denk karşılığı vermekle yetinmeyip bunun üzerine çıkmayı gerektirir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Toplu kaynak anlatımı eylemi iki ana yönde verir: bir başkasına yarar sağlayan iyilik ve kişinin yaptığı işi iyi yürütmesi. Bir şeyi güzelleştirme, kötülüğün karşıtı olan iyi davranış ve denk karşılığın üstüne çıkan verme de bu çerçevede yer alır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Dal çerçevesi, kaynak söz öbeğinin kişiyi sevindiren iyilik, bolluk, iyi karşılık ve iyi son anlamlarını doğru biçimde toplar. Sonsuz mutluluk yurdu, utkı ve inancı uğruna ölme belirli iyi sonuçlar olarak kalmalı; dalın tamamı yalnızca bu örneklere veya güzel bir niteliğe indirgenmemelidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal, bir şeyi güzel kılan niteliği ya da iyilik etme eylemini değil, kişiye ulaşan iyi şeyi, karşılığı veya sonucu bildirir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Genel olarak kişiye ulaşan iyilik ve iyi sonuç bildiren tek sözcüklü biçimler ile iki iyi sonuçtan birini anlatan kalıplaşmış söz öbeği ayrı tutulmalı; bu söz öbeğinin ikili sınırı bütün dala yayılmamalıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişiyi sevindiren iyilik, bolluk, iyi karşılık veya kötü bir şeyin karşısında yer alan iyi sonuçtur. Belirli kullanımlarda sonsuz mutluluk yurdu, utkı ya da inancı uğruna ölme gibi iyi sonları gösterir; iki seçenekli kalıplaşmış kullanım ise yalnızca son iki sonucu birlikte sınırlar.

facets.statement: Kişiye ulaşan ve onu sevindiren iyilik, iyi karşılık veya iyi sonuç, kötü şeyin ve kötü sonun karşıtıdır.
Bolluk, geniş geçim ve utkı, kişinin dünyadaki yaşamında karşılaştığı sevindirici iyi sonuçlar olarak bu dala girer.
İyi bir karşılık veya ödül, sonsuz mutluluk yurduyla örneklenen olumlu son biçimini alabilir.
İki iyi sonuçtan birini bildiren kalıplaşmış kullanım, seçenekleri utkı ile kişinin inancı uğruna ölmesiyle sınırlar.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynakların toplu anlatımı, kötü şeyin karşısındaki sevindirici iyiliği hem dünyadaki bolluk ve utkı hem de ödül ve iyi son olarak verir. Sonsuz mutluluk yurdu ile iki iyi sonuçtan biri olan utkı veya inanç uğruna ölüm, genel çekirdeğin belirli gerçekleşmeleridir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Dal, kaynak söz öbeğindeki dağ, kum sırtı ve kum tepesi gibi yer adlandırmalarını doğru yakalar; ancak kaynak aynı kümede ön kolun bileğe yakın yarısını, ayı, yüksek dağı ve temiz yüksek bir kum tepesine oturma eylemini de verir. Bu nedenle dal tek bir yer veya nesne türü gibi değil, birbiriyle aynı biçim ailesini paylaşan kalıplaşmış gönderimler ve bunlara bağlı bir eylem kullanımı olarak tanımlanmalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal belirli bir söz öbeğiyle sınırlı sayılmamalı; tek sözcüklü biçimlerde kalıplaşmış birden çok gönderimi ve kum tepesine oturmayı bildiren bağlantılı eylem kullanımını kapsamalıdır.

concept_map.definition: Aynı söz ailesindeki biçimlerin dağ, kum sırtı, kum tepesi, ön kolun bileğe yakın yarısı, ay ve yüksek dağ için kalıplaşmış adlandırmalar olarak kullanıldığı; ayrıca temiz ve yüksek bir kum tepesine oturma eylemini bildirdiği söz varlığı kümesidir.

facets.statement: Belirli bir dağ, kum sırtı, kumluk veya temiz yüksek kum tepesi bu söz ailesindeki biçimlerle adlandırılabilir.
Ön kolun bileğe yakın yarısı için kalıplaşmış bir beden bölümü adlandırması bulunur.
Söz ailesindeki ayrı bir biçim ayı adlandırır.
Söz ailesindeki küçültmeli bir biçim, yüksek dağ anlamında kullanılır.
Bağlantılı eylem biçimi, temiz ve yüksek bir kum tepesine oturmayı bildirir.

branches.source_phrase_ar: الحسن جبل وحبل من حبال الرمل (maqayis)؛ الحسن من الذراع النصف الذي يلي الكوع (maqayis)؛ حسن اسم رملة لنبي سعد (ayn)؛ الحاسن القمر (sihah)؛ الحسن اسم رملة لبنى سعد (sihah)؛ الحسن نقا في ديار بني تميم (tahdhib)؛ أحسن الرجل إذا جلس على الحسن وهو الكثيب النقي العالي (tahdhib)؛ الحسين الجبل العالي (tahdhib)

identity_judgment.rationale: Dal çerçevesi, kaynak söz öbeğinde iki kalıplaşmış biçim için verilen bir işi yapmadaki en yüksek çaba ve erişilebilen son sınır anlamını doğru korur. Anlam genel güzellik, kişi adı veya yer adı değildir; yalnızca bu özel ifadelerin bir kişiye bağlanan güç ve son nokta değerlendirmesidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal yalnızca iki kalıplaşmış ifadeye bağlıdır; genel çaba, genel amaç veya her türlü son nokta anlamına genişletilmemelidir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal yalın bir kök anlamı değildir; anlam, kişinin belirli bir işi yaparken gösterebileceği en yüksek çaba ve erişebileceği son sınırı bildiren iki kalıplaşmış biçimle sınırlıdır.

concept_map.definition: Bir kişinin belirli bir işi yapmak için gösterebileceği en yüksek çabayı ve erişebileceği son sınırı bildiren, iki kalıplaşmış biçime özgü anlatımdır.

facets.statement: Belirli bir işi yapmada kişiye ait en yüksek çaba ile ulaşılabilecek son sınır birlikte anlatılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortaklaştırılacak çok kaynaklı bir anlatım yoktur; dal, aynı anlama gelen iki kalıplaşmış biçimin tek tanıklığına dayanır.

source_details.summary: İki kalıplaşmış biçim de bir kişinin belirli bir işteki en yüksek çabasını ve erişebileceği son sınırı bildirir.

concept_gloss.text: bir işteki en yüksek çabası ve erişebileceği son sınır
concept_gloss.applicability: Yalnızca kanıtlanan iki kalıplaşmış biçimde, kişinin belirli bir işi yapma gücünün ve çabasının üst sınırı anlatılırken kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kişiye bağlı çabayı, belirli işi, en yüksek dereceyi ve erişilebilen son sınırı korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Bir kişinin belirli bir işi yapmak için kullanabileceği bütün gücün vurgulandığı doğal anlatımda uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Kişiye bağlı güç ve çabanın erişebildiği en yüksek dereceyi korur.
error_profile.loses: Çabanın yanında ayrıca belirtilen erişilecek son sınırı açıkça adlandırmaz.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Kişinin belli bir işi yaparken hem harcayabileceği çabanın hem ulaşabileceği noktanın üst sınırı açıklanırken kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Gücü, etkin çabayı ve ulaşılabilecek son sınırı tek anlatımda korur.

error_profile.loses: Sınırın belirli bir kişiye ve onun bir işi yaparken göstereceği en yüksek çabaya bağlı olduğunu göstermez.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dalın kalıplaşmış biçimleri, kişinin belirli bir işi yapmadaki en yüksek çabasını ve erişebileceği sınırı bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dalın kalıplaşmış biçimleri, ulaşılması övülen bir sonu ve varılacak en ileri noktayı bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da kalıplaşmış bir anlatımla erişilebilecek en ileri noktayı belirtir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dalda sınır kişinin gücü ve çabasıyla ölçülür; komşuda ise varılan sonun övülmeye değer oluşu öne çıkar. Bu değerlendirme farkı nedeniyle yalnızca son sınır bağlamında yaklaşırlar.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal iki kalıplaşmış biçimde çaba ile erişilebilen son sınırı birlikte bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, belirli bir kalıba bağlı olmadan çalışıp çabalama ve güç harcamayı bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Bir işi yapmak için kişinin gücünü kullanması ve çaba göstermesi iki dalın ortak alanıdır.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal çaba sürecini genel olarak anlatır. Bu dal ise yalnızca özel biçimlerde, o çabanın ulaşabileceği en yüksek dereceyi ve son sınırı birlikte gösterir.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal, kişinin bir işi yaparken harcadığı en yüksek çabayı sınırla birlikte öne çıkarır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, genel güç yetirme alanını, yetmezliği ve ölçünün aşılmasını da kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Bir kişinin bir işi yapabilecek gücü ile erişebileceği sınır iki dalda da değerlendirilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal özel bir anlatımla en yüksek çaba ve son sınırı bildirir. Komşu dal ise genel yeterlik, alan darlığı, yetersizlik ve ölçüyü aşma gibi daha geniş durumlara uzanır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal iki kalıplaşmış biçimde kişinin bir işteki en yüksek çabası ile erişim sınırını birlikte verir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, güçlük altında bütün gücü kullanmayı ve iş, görüş veya yemin gibi daha geniş alanlarda sona varmayı kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Bir işi sonuçlandırmak için bütün gücün kullanılması ve sona kadar çabalanması iki dalda örtüşür.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dal güçlük ve bütün gücü harcama sürecini genel alanlara yayar. Bu dalın anlamı ise iki özel biçimde kişisel çaba ile erişilen üst sınırın birlikte söylenmesine bağlıdır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Bu dal, son sınırı bir kişinin belirli işi yapmadaki gücü ve çabasıyla ilişkilendirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, bir şeyin genel bitişini, kenarını veya bir iletinin ya da okun hedefe ulaşmasını bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: bir şeyin vardığı son ve bitiş
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal da erişilen son noktayı veya üst sınırı anlatabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Komşu dalın çekirdeği nesnenin ya da hareketin vardığı genel sondur. Bu dalda ise sınır, belirli bir kişinin işi yapma çabasının ve gücünün ölçüsüdür.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, akciğerli bir canlının gövdesine havanın girip çıkmasını ve bu döngünün tek tek sayılabilmesini doğrudan anlatır. İçme sırasında sayılan soluklar da bu bedensel sürecin özel bir bağlamıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam, canlı solunumuyla sınırlıdır; can, kan, öz varlık ya da sıkıntı giderme anlamlarını içermez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak dal, soluk alıp verme sürecini bildirir; içme bağlamı yalnızca bu sürecin sayıldığı bir kullanımdır.

concept_map.definition: Akciğerli bir canlının havayı ağız ya da burun yoluyla gövdesine alıp yeniden dışarı vermesidir. Her bir giriş-çıkış döngüsü ayrı bir soluk olarak sayılabilir.

facets.statement: Havanın ağız ya da burun yoluyla gövdeye girip yeniden çıkmasıdır.
İçme sırasında verilen her ara soluk, aynı solunum döngüsünün sayılan bir örneğidir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar, temel anlamı havanın canlı gövdesine girip çıkması ve bu hareketin tekil döngüler hâlinde sayılması olarak ortaklaştırır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Canlının havayı içine alıp dışarı verdiği temel bedensel süreç için kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Havanın gövdeye girişini ve yeniden çıkışını birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Solunumun ya da içme sırasında verilen aranın tek bir döngü olarak sayıldığı yerde uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Tek bir giriş-çıkış döngüsünün sayılabilirliğini korur.

lexical_glosses.target_gloss: tek soluk ya da soluklanma arası

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal, sessiz ve olağan hava girişini de kapsayan tam solunum döngüsüdür.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal, göğüsten havayı dışarı vermeye, buna eşlik eden sese ve sıkıntı belirtisine ağırlık verir.
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dalda da gövdedeki havanın dışarı çıkması bulunur.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal hava alma ile vermeyi birlikte içeren genel solunumdur; komşu ise özellikle güçlü dışa verişi ve doğan sesi anlatır.
